title: Attachment Styles in Relationships
shortDefinition: The unconscious patterns and expectations we develop about emotional closeness, safety, and dependence in relationships.
dailyExample: Feeling intense panic when a partner takes four hours to reply to a text (Anxious) vs. pulling away and shutting down emotionally when someone asks for vulnerability (Avoidant).
psychologyTheory: Developed by John Bowlby and Mary Ainsworth. Attachment styles originate in early infant-caregiver dynamics and create internal working models: Secure, Anxious-Preoccupied, Dismissive-Avoidant, and Fearful-Avoidant.
inTherapy: We explore attachment history to untangle current romantic conflicts, communication breakdowns, and fear of abandonment, moving toward 'Earned Security'.
practicalTakeaway: Your attachment style is a coping strategy, not a life sentence. With insight and conscious practice, insecure patterns can evolve into secure connection.
